I’ve been driving buses for over twenty years, so I’m used to long shifts and stress, but the last three months have been…different.  

I keep getting this strong taste in my mouth, like metal or something rotten, even when I’m just sipping water. It comes out of nowhere, on and off all day, even when I’m relaxed at home watching TV. It makes me suspicious of food sometimes, like something’s wrong with it when everyone else says it’s fine.  

Around the same time, I’ve become convinced my wife is sneaking around on me. There’s no real proof—her phone, her schedule, everything looks normal—but I can’t shake this certainty she’s lying. I check her messages, watch how she talks on the phone, and I know it sounds unreasonable, but it feels undeniably true.  

My wife says I’ve started doing these odd little movements—tapping my fingers in a certain pattern before I open a door, straightening the steering wheel exactly three times before I start the bus. I feel compelled to do them, even if it looks strange.  

I was in a bad crash on my route years ago, but these things don’t feel connected to that. They just started on their own.

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
